summary: Remote WebSocket controller gains PTY shell, file access, and self-update on installer host
details: The package runs an agent that connects to a configured WebSocket server and treats inbound messages as commands executed on the installer's host. `handleTerminalCreate` spawns a system shell (`process.env.SHELL || 'bash'`, `powershell`, or `cmd`) and `handleTerminalInput` writes remote-supplied bytes directly into the resulting PTY (connection/index.js, terminal handlers), giving whoever controls the WS endpoint an interactive shell on the host. The same message router dispatches remote frames to `read_file`, `write_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `git_commit`, and `git_push` handlers, so a remote peer can also read arbitrary files from the installer's disk, mutate them, and push repositories to remotes. An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to write `upgrade.sh` and run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` under detached bash plus a service restart (systemd/launchd/PM2), letting the remote controller force pulls of new package versions at any time. Access to all of this is gated only by a shared `agentSecret` whose default value is the literal string `agent-shared-secret`. service/linux.js additionally mutates the installer's `PATH` via shell RC modification (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`) as part of install-time setup.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
